findings.title: SQL kill switch inverts the flag and always returns false
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions sets enabled to the negation of FlagSqlExpressions and then returns false from both branches, so the flag is never honored and the control flow does not match the function name. This is the only gate on the ExpressionQueryReader SQL path (the error "sqlExpressions is not implemented" at the call site). A reviewer "correcting" the obvious inversion so the fall-through returns true would turn SQL expressions back on whenever the documented feature flag is enabled, which is exactly the CVE-2024-9264 surface. The disablement should be an explicit return false with a comment that SQL expressions are hard-disabled because of that CVE, and it should not read the flag with a negated condition.

findings.title: Disabled SQL expressions report "not implemented"
findings.body: When a SQL expression is rejected, ReadQuery returns fmt.Errorf("sqlExpressions is not implemented"). The feature was implemented and is being turned off to stop RCE/LFI (CVE-2024-9264); the feature flag and its docs are intentionally left in place. Operators who enable that flag, or clients that already send type=sql, will treat this as a missing feature or a bad deploy rather than a security disablement, and may try to turn the flag on or restore DuckDB. The error should say SQL expressions are disabled.

findings.title: No test that SQL expressions cannot reach DuckDB
findings.body: The CVE fix removes go-duck and stubs DB.RunCommands, DB.QueryFramesInto, and DB.TablesList, and rejects QueryTypeSQL in ExpressionQueryReader. Nothing in the change asserts either entry point. UnmarshalSQLCommand/NewSQLCommand still calls sql.TablesList, which still interpolates the user query into SELECT json_serialize_sql('...') and only fails because the stub returns an error; Execute still calls QueryFramesInto. A regression that restores a real in-memory DB, or that drops the reader check, would not be caught. Add a test that both ReadQuery and UnmarshalSQLCommand/Execute reject SQL expressions and never invoke a real engine.
